data.name: Jyaniksha
data.gender_notes: Jyaniksha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jyaniksha is a Sanskrit name, derived from the words ‘jnana’ meaning knowledge and ‘iksha’ meaning inquisitive or insightful. This name is often given to girls who are believed to be deeply knowledgeable and inquisitive by nature. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and learning, is often invoked for the blessings of knowledge and wisdom.
data.spiritual_meaning: May she be blessed with profound knowledge and an inquisitive mind.
data.etymology: Jyaniksha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Knowledgeable, Inquisitive.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jyaniksha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: The name Jyaniksha is mentioned in the 15th-century Sanskrit epic 'Bhagavata Purana'. It is the name of a sage who is described as a great scholar and philosopher. He is also known as Jaimini, and is said to have been the author of the 'Sutras' or 'rules' for the Jaiminiya school of Hindu astrology. Jyaniksha is revered for his deep wisdom and spiritual understanding.

Jyaniksha is believed to have lived around the 3rd or 4th century BCE. He is considered to be one of the seven great sages or 'rishis' of ancient India. According to legend, Jyaniksha was a master of the Vedas and the Upanishads, and was renowned for his extensive knowledge of astronomy and astrology. He is said to have composed several important works on these subjects, including the 'Brihat Parasara Hora Shastra'.
